# FAQ

Purpose: short answers to common questions about Longstead. Each answer points to the guide with details.

## Privacy and data

**1. Does the app send my financial information anywhere?**
Not by default. Your profile, accounts, plans and chats stay on your device, and by default the AI runs on the device. On its own, the app contacts a third-party site only for model downloads you start (from huggingface.co) and, only if you enter your own feed address, tax-table checks to that address. Neither carries your plan data. If you connect your own model server, your questions go to that server (see question 31 below). See [PRIVACY_AND_DATA.md](PRIVACY_AND_DATA.md).

**2. Do I need an account or to sign in?**
No. There is no account, no ads, no analytics and no tracking.

**3. Does it work offline?**
Yes. Calculations, the simulation, and your plans work without internet. Apple's on-device model works offline. A downloaded model works offline once downloaded. You need internet only to download a model or to check for updated tax tables. A model server you connect works only while the app can reach it.

**4. Is my data in my iPhone or iCloud backup?**
No. The app marks its data folder as excluded from backup. Export your plans from **Profile > Plan management > Export plan...** to keep copies, and use them to move to a new device. See [PRIVACY_AND_DATA.md](PRIVACY_AND_DATA.md).

**5. How do I delete everything?**
Use **Settings > Your data > Erase all data...** (it asks for confirmation and cannot be undone), or on iPhone delete the app. On Mac you can also move the app to the Trash and delete `~/Library/Application Support/RetirementPlanner`. You can also delete a plan, a chat, an account, or a model individually. See [PRIVACY_AND_DATA.md](PRIVACY_AND_DATA.md).

**6. Is the exported .retplan file protected?**
No. It is plain text containing your name, ages and balances. Keep it somewhere private.

## Getting started

**7. What do I need to run it?**
iPhone with iOS 27 or later, or a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 26 or later. See [QUICK_START.md](QUICK_START.md) and [MAC_INSTALLATION.md](MAC_INSTALLATION.md).

**8. Do I need Apple Intelligence?**
No. If your device has it, the advisors can use Apple's model with no download. If not, download an open-source model from **Settings > Manage models**, or connect your own model server. See [AI_AND_MODELS.md](AI_AND_MODELS.md).

**9. Does it work on iPad?**
The app contains an iPad layout with a sidebar, but it has not yet been checked on a physical iPad. The version being distributed first is for iPhone (through TestFlight) and Mac.

**10. How do I get the Mac version? Is it on the Mac App Store?**
It is a signed and notarized download from the publisher's website and GitHub Releases, not the Mac App Store. See [MAC_INSTALLATION.md](MAC_INSTALLATION.md).

**11. Do I need Ollama?**
No. Apple's built-in model works with nothing to install, and you can download an open-source model instead. Ollama is optional: if it is running on your computer, the app finds it (at `http://localhost:11434`), connects, and sets each advisor's default model for you. You can undo that with **Use Apple's built-in model instead** in the chat header. See [AI_AND_MODELS.md](AI_AND_MODELS.md).

**12. Can I use my own server?**
Yes. In **Settings > Your own model server** choose Ollama, LM Studio, or Other (any server that speaks the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` chat API), then tap **Connect and test**. Then set advisors to use it. See [SETTINGS_GUIDE.md](SETTINGS_GUIDE.md) and [AI_AND_MODELS.md](AI_AND_MODELS.md).

## Plan, simulation and numbers

**13. What does "plan health 82%" mean?**
Of the simulated futures, 82% kept your money from running out before your horizon age. It is a scenario estimate, not a probability you can rely on and not a guarantee. See [USER_GUIDE.md](USER_GUIDE.md).

**14. Does plan health change each time I run it?**
The simulation draws random market returns, but with a fixed random seed: the same plan gives the same result every time. It changes only when your plan or a slider changes.

**15. Why is my plan health 0%?**
Usually no accounts have been added, spending is much larger than your savings and Social Security, or retirement age is early. See [TROUBLESHOOTING.md](TROUBLESHOOTING.md).

**16. Are the numbers in today's dollars?**
Yes. The Simulate screen uses real (inflation-adjusted) dollars: your spending stays constant in today's dollars and returns are real returns. See [GLOSSARY.md](GLOSSARY.md) for real versus nominal.

**17. What return and volatility does it assume?**
They start from your risk tolerance: 3% return and 8% volatility (Conservative), 5% and 12% (Moderate), or 7% and 16% (Aggressive). You can change them with sliders; the sliders are left alone until you change your risk tolerance again.

**18. Does my account's "Expected return" matter?**
It is stored but the Simulate screen does not use it (it uses your risk tolerance for the whole portfolio). One return assumption applies to the whole portfolio.

**19. When do RMDs start?**
At 73 if you were born before 1960, and at 75 if you were born in 1960 or later (SECURE 2.0). The app estimates your birth year from your current age.

**20. How should I enter Social Security?**
Enter the monthly benefit you expect at the age you plan to claim, and set the claim age (62 to 70). The Simulate and Withdraw screens use the number as entered, without adjusting for early or late claiming. The advisors' claiming comparison treats the number as your full-retirement-age benefit. See [USER_GUIDE.md](USER_GUIDE.md).

**21. Which states are supported?**
You can choose any of the 50 states or DC (stored as a two-letter code). State income tax tables are bundled for California, New York, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Texas, Florida, Washington, Nevada and New Jersey (2025 tables). States with no income tax (AK, FL, NV, NH, SD, TN, TX, WA, WY) are correctly zero. For any other state the app warns that tables are not included yet and shows federal tax only.

**22. Does it calculate IRMAA, NIIT, AMT, or early-withdrawal penalties?**
No. See "What the app does not model" in [USER_GUIDE.md](USER_GUIDE.md).

**23. Is an account's tax treatment set automatically?**
It pre-fills from the account type (for example Roth accounts become Tax-Free, HSAs Tax-Exempt, brokerage Taxable) until you pick one yourself, and editing never overwrites your choice. Check it for unusual accounts, because withdrawal order and RMDs depend on it.

**24. How do I compare "retire at 62" with my current plan?**
Open **Profile > Plan management > Duplicate plan**, change the retirement age in the copy, save, and run **Simulate** on each plan (switch plans from the Plan tab). Or change only the retirement-age slider on **Simulate**, which does not alter your saved profile.

**25. Why is "Your picture" collapsed in the sidebar?**
On Mac and iPad, "Your picture" starts collapsed so the sidebar stays short. It shows an "N more" chip: click the chip or the arrow to expand it. Inside are Plan, Debts, Income, Other assets, Goals, Dependents, Assumptions, Reports, Stress test and Scenarios. See [USER_GUIDE.md](USER_GUIDE.md).

**26. Can I export a PDF of my plan?**
No. Plans export as `.retplan` files for backup or moving to another device. You can export a single advisor conversation (chat menu > Export conversation...) as Markdown, shared text, or a PDF.

## AI advisors

**27. Does the advisor remember what I just asked?**
Only briefly: it remembers your last two exchanges in the chat (each shortened), so short follow-ups work. Anything older, or anything in a cleared thread, is forgotten. Repeat the details (year, filing status, state, amounts) for important questions. See [AI_AND_MODELS.md](AI_AND_MODELS.md).

**28. What does "Some figures were not computed by the planner's tools" mean?**
Those numbers in the answer were not produced by the app's calculators and were not in your message or profile, so the app could not verify them. Ask again with more detail or ask the Tax Consultant to compute them.

**29. Why do the advisors' success numbers differ from the Simulate screen?**
They should not: plan figures in chat come from the same planning engine as Simulate (10,000 trials, fixed random seed). If you see a difference, check whether you moved the Simulate sliders (retirement age, return, volatility, horizon), which do not change your saved profile.

**30. Which model should I download?**
Use the one marked recommended. On an iPhone with 8 GB or 12 GB of memory it is Qwen3.5 4B (3.0 GB), and on a 4 GB iPhone Qwen3.5 2B (1.7 GB). On an iPad, and on a Mac with under 48 GB, it is Qwen3.5 9B (6.0 GB). On a Mac with 48 GB or more it is Qwen3.5 35B-A3B (20.4 GB). See [AI_AND_MODELS.md](AI_AND_MODELS.md).

**31. Is my data sent anywhere when I use the AI?**
With Apple's built-in model or a downloaded model, no: the question is answered on your device. If an advisor is set to your own model server, what the model sees is sent to that server. A local address (`localhost`, `127.x`, `*.local`, `10.x`, `172.16` to `172.31.x`, `192.168.x`) is treated as your own computer or network; any other address shows a warning. Requests to your server appear in **Settings > Network audit log**. The app contains no cloud AI service of its own, and Private Cloud Compute is off.

**32. Why does my plan number not change between models?**
The AI does not do the math. Plan numbers (the chance your savings last, median ending balance, net worth, debts, income) come from the app's planning engine, which uses a fixed random seed, so the same plan gives the same number whichever model is answering. For the Retirement Planner advisor, the app checks every dollar amount and percentage in the reply against the engine's figures. **My plan numbers (no AI)** in the Retirement Planner chat shows the engine's figures with no model at all.

**33. Can the AI read my bank statements or PDFs?**
No. There is no way to attach a file or photo in this version.

**34. Is the AI's answer financial advice?**
No. It can be wrong. Check important figures and consult a qualified professional.

## Settings and updates

**35. What does "Allow yearly tax-data updates" do?**
It matters only if you have entered your own tax-data feed address in Settings > Tax data. By default there is no feed and the app makes no tax-data requests; it uses the tax tables built in. See [SETTINGS_GUIDE.md](SETTINGS_GUIDE.md).

**36. How do I change the text size?**
**Settings > Display > Text size** on iPhone and Mac. On iPad the app follows the system text size.

**37. How do I update the Mac app?**
Download the newer release, verify it, and replace the app in Applications. Version 1.0 does not update itself. See [MAC_INSTALLATION.md](MAC_INSTALLATION.md).

**38. Why is the app always dark?**
The app uses a dark appearance regardless of the system setting.
